title: security: RBAC v2 KMS region residency enforcement + audit hardening
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: After a recent support escalation (SUP-2381) and an internal review of data residency controls, we observed gaps where customer KMS usages could be routed to a different region than the dataset/tenant residency. This PR hardens RBAC v2 enforcement to ensure KMS region pinning is validated end-to-end and that all KMS key accesses emit structured audit events.

Summary: Implement RBAC v2 enforcement for KMS region residency, add audit logging hooks for KMS operations, add CLI/installer checks, and introduce a two-week audit-only rollout followed by enforcement. The change is configurable via feature flag (rbac_v2_kms_residency_mode = audit|enforce). Default rollout: audit for two weeks, then switch to enforce after monitoring.

What changed (high level):
- Policy enforcer: validate that any request that references a customer-managed KMS key includes a matching kms_region that is allowed by the tenant's residency policy. When in audit mode, violations are logged as structured audit events; when in enforce mode, requests are rejected with 403 and a clear error code.
- Audit logging: added structured audit event fields (kms_key_id, kms_region, tenant_id, enforcement_mode, policy_id, decision, request_id) and a new event type kms_access_policy_violation. Events are emitted to the existing audit pipeline and tagged for retention.
- Private installer & Dedicated: added preflight checks to the installer to validate KMS region configuration and tooling to migrate existing KMS bindings to include region metadata.
- API validation: service-side validation for Create/Update resource paths that reference KMS keys; improved error messages and retry guidance.
- Tests: unit, integration, and e2e tests covering audit and enforce modes; test fixtures for cross-region KMS keys.
- Docs: new doc on KMS region residency and migration guide.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag default = audit. Deploy to hosted and dedicated clusters. Monitor audit events and alert on violation rate.
2) After 14 days of stable violation rate and remediation playbooks exercised, flip to enforce.
3) Backout: feature flag can switch back to audit immediately if false positives are observed.

Related: ENG-4123 (policy enforcer work), SEC-591 (compliance scope), SUP-2381 (customer incident).

Notes: This PR touches both control-plane and private installer code paths. Care was taken to keep the default behavior non-breaking by shipping audit-only first. See release notes for admin action items.

Asha Patel (author): Updated schema to include policy_id and enforcement_mode, normalized field names to snake_case. Left a compatibility shim for older audit consumers.
Priya Nair (reviewer): Integration tests failed in CI with a missing KMS_TEST_REGION env; add a fallback for CI runs. Also consider rate-limiting the audit event emission to avoid saturation.
Asha Patel (author): Added CI fallback and a token-bucket limiter for audit event emission (configurable). Re-ran tests locally and in CI.

Omar Ruiz (security): Add a migration plan for existing tenants that have KMS references without region metadata. Confirmed installer script will annotate existing bindings and emit audit alerts. Approving pending a short docs section for SRE runbooks.

release_notes:
- Enforceable RBAC v2 predicate for KMS region residency; configurable mode (audit|enforce)
- Structured audit events for KMS policy violations (kms_access_policy_violation)
- Installer preflight and migration helper to annotate existing KMS bindings with region metadata
- Admin action: monitor audit events and flip feature flag to enforce after validation
notes_for_admins: Default rollout is audit-only. Admins should watch observability-pack/alerts/kms_audit_violation_rate.yml and follow the migration guide in redwood-docs/security/kms_region_residency.md before flipping to enforce mode.
testing_notes: Added unit, integration, and e2e tests. In CI we included a fallback KMS_TEST_REGION to avoid false negatives. Tests cover audit and enforce modes and the installer migration flow.
